description: Arbor milling (often referred to as horizontal milling or gang milling using an arbor) is a Mass-Reducing (Subtractive) machining process. It utilizes a rotating, multi-tooth peripheral milling cutter mounted on a rigid horizontal shaft (the arbor) supported by an overarm, making contact with a workpiece to remove material in the form of chips via mechanical shear.

name: Gear Hobbing
summary: Gear hobbing is a continuous gear-generating machining process used to cut teeth into cylindrical blanks (spurs, helices, splines, and worm gears) using a…
description: Gear hobbing is a continuous gear-generating machining process used to cut teeth into cylindrical blanks (spurs, helices, splines, and worm gears) using a specialized rotating cutting tool called a hob. The hob and the workpiece rotate simultaneously in a synchronized kinematic relationship, creating teeth through progressive, incremental chip removal.

name: Band Filing
summary: Band filing is a continuous, mass-reducing machining process that utilizes a flexible, continuous steel band fitted with interlocking file segments (a file…
description: Band filing is a continuous, mass-reducing machining process that utilizes a flexible, continuous steel band fitted with interlocking file segments (a file band) to remove material from a workpiece. Running continuously in one direction over upper and lower wheels on a band machining frame, it provides uniform, unidirectional filing action for contouring, deburring, and precise surface finishing.

name: Band Sawing
summary: Band sawing is a continuous mass-reducing (machining/cutting) manufacturing process that uses a long, flexible, continuous loop of serrated metal blade (a…
description: Band sawing is a continuous mass-reducing (machining/cutting) manufacturing process that uses a long, flexible, continuous loop of serrated metal blade (a saw band) stretched between two or more rotating wheels to cut material.

name: Broaching
summary: Broaching is a high-precision, high-efficiency machining process that uses a multi-toothed cutting tool (a broach) to progressively remove material from a…
description: Broaching is a high-precision, high-efficiency machining process that uses a multi-toothed cutting tool (a broach) to progressively remove material from a workpiece in a single linear or rotary pass. As the tool advances, each successive tooth rises slightly higher than the previous one (Rise Per Tooth), shaping the workpiece to the exact inverse geometry of the tool.

name: Centerless Grinding
summary: Centerless grinding is an abrasive mass-reducing machining process used to remove material from cylindrical or tubular workpieces without using a spindle or…
description: Centerless grinding is an abrasive mass-reducing machining process used to remove material from cylindrical or tubular workpieces without using a spindle or centers to fix and locate the part. The workpiece is supported on a work-rest blade and held between a high-speed grinding wheel and a slower-speed regulating wheel.

name: Circular Sawing
summary: A mechanical mass-reducing (subtractive) manufacturing process that utilizes a powered rotating circular disk blade—equipped with teeth or coated with…
description: A mechanical mass-reducing (subtractive) manufacturing process that utilizes a powered rotating circular disk blade—equipped with teeth or coated with abrasive particles—to shear or abrade a narrow channel (kerf) through a workpiece, separating material or trimming stock to required dimensions.

name: Conventional Blanking
summary: Conventional blanking is a high-volume, mass-reducing mechanical shearing process used to cut flat, closed-contour geometric shapes ("blanks") out of sheet…
description: Conventional blanking is a high-volume, mass-reducing mechanical shearing process used to cut flat, closed-contour geometric shapes ("blanks") out of sheet metal stock using a punch and die set installed in a mechanical or hydraulic press. The punched-out piece is the desired product, while the remaining sheet metal is scrap.

name: Cylindrical Grinding
summary: A precision abrasive material removal process used to shape and finish the external or internal cylindrical surfaces of metallic, ceramic, or composite…
description: A precision abrasive material removal process used to shape and finish the external or internal cylindrical surfaces of metallic, ceramic, or composite workpieces. The process operates through micro-cutting and erosion action as a high-speed rotating abrasive grinding wheel engages with a rotating workpiece.

name: Die Threading
summary: Die Threading is a traditional mass-reducing (machining) process used to cut external screw threads on the outside surface of a cylindrical workpiece (such…
description: Die Threading is a traditional mass-reducing (machining) process used to cut external screw threads on the outside surface of a cylindrical workpiece (such as rods, bolts, or pipes). It uses a specialized cutting tool called a "die" with internal cutting edges or teeth corresponding to the desired thread profile.

name: Drilling
summary: A mass-reducing (subtractive), mechanical machining process that uses a rotating cutting tool (drill bit) to produce or enlarge a circular hole in a solid…
description: A mass-reducing (subtractive), mechanical machining process that uses a rotating cutting tool (drill bit) to produce or enlarge a circular hole in a solid workpiece. The tool applies axial thrust force ($F_z$) and rotational torque ($M_z$) to shear away material in the form of chips through mechanical fracture and plastic deformation along the main cutting edges.

name: End Milling
summary: End milling is a versatile subtractive (mass-reducing, mechanical, contact) manufacturing process where a rotating cylindrical cutting tool with cutting…
description: End milling is a versatile subtractive (mass-reducing, mechanical, contact) manufacturing process where a rotating cylindrical cutting tool with cutting teeth (flutes) on both its peripheral surface and flat/radiused end face removes material from a stationary or moving workpiece to produce flat surfaces, slots, pockets, complex contours, and 3D profiles.

name: Fine Blanking
summary: Fine blanking is a specialized high-precision sheet metal forming/shearing process that produces fully sheared, flat edges with smooth surfaces, no edge…
description: Fine blanking is a specialized high-precision sheet metal forming/shearing process that produces fully sheared, flat edges with smooth surfaces, no edge fracture, and tight dimensional tolerances in a single press stroke. Unlike conventional blanking, it completely eliminates die roll and break-out zones by applying triple-action mechanical/hydraulic clamping forces (a V-ring impingement ring outside the shear line and a counter-punch inside the shear line) against the main punch during cutting with extremely tight die clearances.

name: Gear Shaping
summary: A traditional material-removal (machining) manufacturing process used to generate gear teeth, splines, and keyways. It uses a reciprocating, circular…
description: A traditional material-removal (machining) manufacturing process used to generate gear teeth, splines, and keyways. It uses a reciprocating, circular pinion-shaped (or rack-shaped) cutting tool that rotates in synchronized motion with the cylindrical gear blank.

name: Honing
summary: Honing is an abrasive machining process that produces a high-precision, low-roughness surface on a metal workpiece by rubbing an expanding abrasive stone or…
description: Honing is an abrasive machining process that produces a high-precision, low-roughness surface on a metal workpiece by rubbing an expanding abrasive stone or set of sticks against it along a controlled dual-motion (rotational and reciprocating) path. It is primarily used to finish internal cylindrical surfaces (bores) to achieve tight geometric tolerances (roundness, straightness, cylindrical taper) and a specific cross-hatch surface texture required for lubrication retention.
